summary:
What we developed: KisanSignal is a multilingual web app that turns NASA satellite data and ground sensor readings into simple, farm-level signals. It combines NASA POWER (weather and solar), GPM (rainfall), SMAP (soil moisture), MODIS (vegetation), and SoilSCAPE (in-field soil sensors). Seven views (Today, Act, Farm, History, Map, Sensors, Share) take a farmer from current conditions to a clear next step they can share with others.
How it addresses the challenge: Valuable Earth observation data is scattered across portals and hard for farmers to interpret. KisanSignal brings it together on one map and translates it into plain guidance for a specific field. It supports 13 languages, 21 country codes, 7 currencies, and hectare or acre units, so the information fits each farmer's local context.
Why it matters: Smallholder farmers face rising weather and water uncertainty, yet rarely have access to space-based insights. By making this data local, understandable, and usable on any phone, KisanSignal helps farmers make timely decisions about irrigation, planting, and risk, supporting better yields and food security.
details:
What it does and how it works

KisanSignal is a web app that gives a farmer a clear, local view of their field. A user picks their location and the app combines NASA satellite data with ground sensor readings:

NASA POWER for weather and solar data

GPM for rainfall

SMAP for soil moisture

MODIS for vegetation

SoilSCAPE for in-field soil sensors

Seven views present it: Today, Act, Farm, History, Map, Sensors, and Share. Results appear on an OpenStreetMap-based map.

Benefits

One place for data that is normally scattered across portals

Plain guidance for a specific field instead of raw datasets

Works on a phone through the browser, with no install

Matches the farmer's context: 13 languages, hectare or acre, and 7 currencies (₹, $, €, £, KSh, ₦, ৳)

Intended impact

Give smallholder farmers in India, Africa, Southeast Asia, and Latin America access to space-based insights, so they can time irrigation, planting, and risk decisions better. The aim is higher yields, less wasted water and inputs, and stronger food security.

Tools and technology

Visible from the live app: NASA Earth observation datasets, OpenStreetMap, and hosting on Render. [Add your own: frontend framework, backend language, APIs, and any AI tools used. I can't see this from the public page.]

Creativity

Turns complex Earth science into a simple signal-and-action flow

Treats localization as a core feature (language, currency, land units, 21 country codes), not an afterthought

Pairs satellite data with real in-field sensors

Factors considered

Accessibility for low-literacy and multilingual users

Mobile-first design for low-cost phones

Data reliability, by using established NASA sources

Local relevance, through units and currency

Shareability, so advice can reach family, neighbors, or extension workers
